title: Federated Republic of Mexico
capsule: The First Mexican Republic was established by the Constitution of 1824, which created a federal system modeled partly on the United States, with Guadalupe Victoria inaugurated as the first president. The republic was plagued by chronic fiscal crisis, regional revolts, and the contest between Federalists and Centralists; the Texas Revolution of 1836 resulted in the loss of Texas, and the republic's federalist constitution was suspended repeatedly. Santa Anna's centralist coup in 1835–1836 effectively ended the first federal experiment; after further upheavals, a new Federal Constitution was restored in 1857, but the period attested in the dataset (1824–1865) encompasses both the First Republic and the Reform War era.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Mexican national territory in this period is documented through the 1824 constitution and subsequent state boundaries; the northern frontier with the United States was contested and redefined by the Treaties of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) and the Gadsden Purchase (1853), making pre-1848 geometry approximate for those regions.
